<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged experiment and determine whether it is healthy. Inspect the
source, launch script, metrics, rollouts and debug evidence. If you find a
defect, repair it in `/workspace`. Do not launch training; the system performs
the graded rerun after your response. Cheap non-training checks are allowed.

Write `/workspace/report.md` describing the root cause, every changed file and
the expected metric effect. A missing report scores zero.

The system deletes `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then runs:

```bash
bash run_experiment.sh
```

The fixed experiment must preserve the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8
bundle, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32,
temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU
layout. Do not add format reward or any auxiliary reward, and do not alter
data, model, budget or metric logging. The grader reads only fresh files under
`experiment_logs`: the final step-4 actor/rollout health metric, cross-checked
against verl's own per-step file log and the probe dumps the run writes, with
the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256. Copying or
fabricating metrics scores zero.
I’ll inspect the experiment code, launch script, and recorded run evidence, then repair any defect and write `/workspace/report.md`. I’ll use only non-training checks.

def load_functions(relative_path, names, namespace, class_name=None):
    path = ROOT / relative_path
    nodes = ast.parse(path.read_text()).body
    if class_name:
        nodes = next(node for node in nodes if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == class_name).body
    selected = [copy.deepcopy(node) for node in nodes if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name in names]
    assert {node.name for node in selected} == set(names)
    for node in selected:
        node.decorator_list = []
    module = ast.Module(body=selected, type_ignores=[])
    exec(compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(module), str(path), 'exec'), namespace)


class Config(dict):
    __getattr__ = dict.__getitem__


class TinyModel(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.q_proj = torch.nn.Linear(16, 16, bias=False)
        self.v_proj = torch.nn.Linear(16, 16, bias=False)
        self.k_proj = torch.nn.Linear(16, 16, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.q_proj(x) + self.v_proj(x) + self.k_proj(x)

         'fsdp_version': lambda module: 0}

load_functions('verl/verl/utils/fsdp_utils.py', ['collect_lora_params', 'replace_lora_wrapper'], utils)


class Rollout:
    def __init__(self, sleep_level):
        self.sleep_level = sleep_level
        self.base = {}
        self.adapter = {}
        self.calls = []

    async def resume(self, tags):
        self.calls.append(('resume', tags))

    async def update_weights(self, weights, peft_config=None, base_sync_done=False):
        values = {key: value.detach().clone() for key, value in weights}
        if peft_config is not None and base_sync_done:
            self.calls.append(('adapter', values))
            self.adapter = values
        else:
            self.calls.append(('base', values))
            self.base = values

    def forward(self, x, peft_config):
        result = torch.zeros_like(x)
        for name in ['q_proj', 'v_proj', 'k_proj']:
            weight = self.base[name + '.base_layer.weight']
            if name in peft_config.target_modules:
                prefix = 'base_model.model.' + name
                a = self.adapter[prefix + '.lora_A.weight']
                b = self.adapter[prefix + '.lora_B.weight']
                weight = weight + b @ a * (peft_config.lora_alpha / peft_config.r)
            result = result + torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight)
        return result

async def check_sync(sleep_level, initially_synced):
    torch.manual_seed(2026)
    actor = get_peft_model(TinyModel(), LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=8, target_modules=['q_proj', 'v_proj'], init_lora_weights='pissa_niter_2'))
    actor.eval()
    ref_cfg = copy.deepcopy(actor.peft_config['default'])
    ref_cfg.init_lora_weights = False
    ref_cfg.inference_mode = True
    actor.add_adapter('_base_ref', ref_cfg)
    actor.set_adapter('default')
    config = Config(rollout=Config(layered_summon=False, free_cache_engine=True), model=Config(path='residual_base', lora_adapter_path='pissa_adapter'))
    rollout = Rollout(sleep_level)
    if initially_synced:
        base = utils['collect_lora_params'](actor, False, False)
        rollout.base = {utils['replace_lora_wrapper'](name, actor.peft_config['default']): value.clone() for name, value in base.items()}
    worker = SimpleNamespace(actor_module_fsdp=actor, _is_offload_param=False, _is_svd_init=True,
                             _is_lora=True, base_sync_done=initially_synced, rank=1, config=config,
                             layered_summon=False, rollout=rollout, gen_random_states=torch.tensor([1]))
    x = torch.randn(2, 16)
    original = {name: value.clone() for name, value in actor.state_dict().items()}
    await namespace['rollout_mode'](worker)
    torch.testing.assert_close(rollout.forward(x, actor.peft_config['default']), actor(x), rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6)
    assert worker.base_sync_done
    assert len(rollout.adapter) == 4 and all('_base_ref' not in name for name in rollout.adapter)
    assert sum(kind == 'base' for kind, _ in rollout.calls) == (0 if initially_synced and sleep_level == 1 else 1)
    for name, value in actor.state_dict().items():
        torch.testing.assert_close(value, original[name], rtol=0, atol=0)
    # Perturb an adapter as a stand-in for a future update; no gradients or optimizer.
    with torch.no_grad():

    assert sum(kind == 'base' for kind, _ in rollout.calls) == (1 if sleep_level == 2 else 0)
    assert sum(kind == 'adapter' for kind, _ in rollout.calls) == 1
    print(f'PASS first/later sync: sleep_level={sleep_level}, initially_synced={initially_synced}')

    engine = Engine(ids)

*** Add File: /workspace/report.md
+# Experiment review and repair
+
+The staged experiment is unhealthy. The defect is in actor-to-vLLM policy synchronization and adapter selection, rather than the supplied PiSSA bundle or the reward function.
+
+## Evidence and root cause
+
+- `observed_run/metrics/all_steps.jsonl` records final step-4 `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.2560474629304847` and `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement = 0.10476375009925555`. The same run has zero training reward, zero advantages and zero gradient norm throughout its four updates, and large rollout/actor discrepancies (`rollout_corr/kl` approximately 2.89–3.57).
+- The recorded rollouts contain incoherent text and repeated tokens; all 48 supplied training generations across steps 1, 2 and 4 receive zero reward. Most responses exhaust the 32-token limit. The console log corroborates the metrics and shows completion of all four steps; its shutdown errors occur after the unhealthy results have already been logged.
+- `observed_run/debug/unknown_exp.rollout_sync_initial.rank0.json` reports `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` with no rollout PEFT config, followed by `lora_delta` in the latest sync dump. This startup path substitutes the original pretrained checkpoint for the configured residual base and does not install the initial adapter.
+- PiSSA requires the effective actor policy to be `W_res + (alpha/r) * B_t @ A_t`. Its initial adapter is nonzero: `W_res + B_0 @ A_0` reconstructs the original pretrained weights here because alpha/r is 1. Loading the original weights as the base and then applying the unchanged PiSSA adapter would count the initial component twice. Loading only the residual weights also serves the wrong policy.
+- Independently, the async server tests the string `VLLM_LORA_NAME` (`"123"`) against the integer IDs returned by `engine.list_loras()` (`{123}`). Consequently generation omits `LoRARequest` even after synchronization installs an adapter. With level-2 sleep, later syncs restore the residual base, but requests then use that residual without its required adapter. This explains the degraded rollouts despite an active actor adapter in the actor debug dumps.
+- Reference computation is already correct: the frozen `_base_ref` adapter reconstructs the initial policy over the residual base. The final reference MAE is 0 and reference consistency is 1. The zero initial actor/reference KL is therefore expected, and zero reward leaves GRPO without an advantage signal; these observations do not independently establish an optimizer defect.
+
+## Every changed file
+
+| File | Change | Expected metric effect |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py` | Remove the original-checkpoint startup branch and its unused loader. Collect the actor's actual residual base; install base weights and the current adapter through separate vLLM updates on the first sync. Continue updating the adapter, and restore the residual base after level-2 sleep. Initialize the transfer device before either transfer path. | Align rollout weights with the actor from the first generation through step 4; sharply reduce actor/rollout MAE and training rollout discrepancies, increasing policy agreement. |
+| `verl/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py` | Check `VLLM_LORA_INT_ID` against registered integer adapter IDs when deciding whether to attach a `LoRARequest`. | Actually use the synchronized adapter during generation, removing the residual-only inference error. Fresh request probes should report adapter ID 123 and `lora_request_used: true`. |
+| `report.md` | Add this diagnosis, change inventory and validation record. | Documentation only; no metric effect. |
+
+The primary expected improvement is a substantially lower final step-4 policy MAE and higher agreement than the recorded 0.1048. Exact agreement of 1 is not promised: actor/vLLM numerical differences and existing temperature handling remain. Base-reference consistency should remain 1, with MAE 0. Coherent rollouts may restore nonzero task rewards and GRPO gradients when sampled answers differ in correctness; no particular accuracy improvement is claimed for this fixed four-update budget.
+
+## Non-training validation
+
+- Python syntax checks passed for both edited modules; `bash -n run_experiment.sh` passed.
+- Eight CPU-only isolated source checks passed. They execute the edited sync/generation methods without initializing a trainer, Ray or a vLLM engine. A tiny real PEFT rank-8 PiSSA model verifies first and subsequent syncs with sleep levels 1 and 2, including a preloaded base and a manually perturbed current adapter. The checks compare effective rollout outputs with actor outputs, verify startup does not mutate actor parameters, and confirm the frozen reference adapter is excluded from synchronization. They also cover the plain full-model path and registered, absent and unrelated adapter IDs during requests. No backward pass or optimizer step was run.
+- Read-only tensor checks covered all 48 q/v projections in the supplied bundle. Every adapter delta is nonzero and rank 8. Mean per-projection absolute error relative to the original pretrained weights is approximately 0.004969 for the residual alone, versus 0.00002532 after adding `B_0 @ A_0`, consistent with the saved bfloat16 rounding.
+- SHA256 checks passed for all 58 unchanged launch, health-trainer, asset, dataset and recorded-evidence files in the initial manifest. The deterministic parquet datasets still contain 16 training and 8 validation rows. AST comparisons confirm reference computations, health/probe writer functions and the rollout-sync probe block are unchanged.
+- Full module imports in the repair container encounter an existing TensorDict dependency mismatch (`LinkedList` missing from `tensordict.utils`).
